summary: Redwood gave a model catalog walkthrough focused on selecting open models for Riverview's clinical summarization and triage use cases. Discussion covered latency/throughput tradeoffs, quantization/compatibility with H100/A100, hosted vs dedicated tradeoffs, and next steps for a 2-week POC. Action items: pricing, benchmarks, compatibility matrix, and VPC/security docs.
transcript:
[00:00] Alex (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for carving some time today. Quick intro, I'm Alex, AE for the healthcare vertical, and with me is Maya Ortiz, our solutions engineer.
[00:12] Maya (Redwood SE): Hi all. We'll run through the model catalog demo, show the benchmark results, and the compatibility matrix - and then leave time for Q&A and next steps.
[00:23] Dr. Sarah (Riverview): Great thanks, excited. We mostly want to understand how to pick models for clinical summarization and triage, and how much ops work this will be.
[00:33] Jorge (Riverview): Also need to know what runs in our VPC vs hosted, and what the latency numbers look like for our 300 RPS burst pattern.
[00:41] Maya: Perfect. Quick agenda - 1) catalog UI + filters 2) demo: pick open models and compare benchmarks 3) compatibility matrix for quantization and hardware 4) Optimize suggestions for batching/caching 5) questions/next steps.
[00:55] Alex: One note on naming - in the UI we surface model families and verified performance profiles; you can filter by task (summarization), license (open), and fidelity.
[01:07] Maya: Ok jumping into the UI - Slides: https://redwood.ai/deck/model-catalog (shared). On the left you can see filters; we'll filter to 'summarization' and 'open models' only.
[01:22] [01:23] Maya: Here we have three recommended families for your use case: LlamaX-13B, Mistral-7B, and an LLM-quant-8B variant we verified. The catalog shows per-model latency at 512 tokens, throughput (tokens/sec), memory footprint, and an entry for compatibility: which quantization modes and GPU types are tested.
[01:40] Dr. Sarah: When you say "verified" what does that mean?
[01:44] Maya: Good question - verified means we ran an internal benchmark harness with representative prompts and token lengths, and measured p50/p95 latency, throughput, and quality via rouge/precision on your sample eval set. We also run quality checks to ensure quantization doesn't degrade critical medical phrasing.
[01:59] Jorge: Do you have numbers for p95 at 512? We care about tail latency.
[02:05] Maya: Yes - example here: LlamaX-13B float FP16 on H100 gives p50 ~120ms p95 ~220ms at 1-stream. With our continuous batching at 8 batch size throughput is ~40k tokens/sec on a 4xH100 pod. The quantized 8-bit variant on A100/FP8-ish profile has p95 ~270-320ms but reduces memory footprint by ~45%.
[02:30] Alex: Important tradeoff - quantization helps you run more concurrent instances on Dedicated or Private, but can increase p95 slightly. We can show a compatibility matrix mapping models -> quantization profile -> supported GPUs (H100, A100, T4) which we will share.
[02:46] [02:50] Maya: Pulling up the compatibility sheet: https://redwood.ai/compatibility/riverview (you're seeing a live view). For example, LlamaX-13B supports Q4_0 and Q8_1 on A100/H100; LLM-quant-8B supports Q4 and runs well on T4 for low-cost inference but with higher latency.
[03:10] Nina (Riverview): Quick ops question - if we run Private in our VPC, can the model variants still use the same quantization profiles or do we need different builds?
[03:20] Maya: Same code paths - quantization profiles are model artifacts and transfer with the model. The runtime picks optimized kernels depending on the GPU and profile. For on-prem the only difference is we validate the binary kernels against your driver stack and provide a validated matrix. Occasionally we see mismatches called out as "KV cash" in older transcriptions - meaning KV cache incompatibilities - but we test KV cache consistency in our matrix.
[03:44] Jorge: For our 300 RPS bursts, do you recommend Hosted or Dedicated?
[03:50] Alex: If you need predictable p95 SLAs and data isolation, Dedicated is the path; Hosted can do bursts but you may see variability during noisy neighbors. We can scope a Dedicated pool size to handle your steady-state plus burst. Using Redwood Optimize we can set autoscale + burst capacity with cost caps.
[04:08] Maya: To illustrate cost/latency tradeoffs, here's a quick benchmark table we ran with a 512-token prompt representing a SOAP note:
[04:18] Maya: - LlamaX-13B FP16 (H100) p95 220ms cost est $0.85 per 1k tokens (hosted)
[04:26] Maya: - LLM-quant-8B Q4 on A100 p95 320ms cost est $0.40 per 1k tokens
[04:33] Maya: - Mistral-7B distilled on T4 p95 480ms cost est $0.20 per 1k tokens (good for lower-cost batch jobs)
[04:40] Dr. Sarah: That delta is clearer. For clinical summarization accuracy, do you have eval numbers?
[04:45] Maya: We used your anonymized sample set you shared and ran ROUGE and clinical-specific checks: LlamaX-13B had best fidelity on named entity preservation; Mistral-7B was close for general summarization but missed some entity-level details. We'll attach the CSV with eval metrics.
[04:59] Alex: We'll also include human-in-the-loop thresholds if you want to route uncertain cases to clinicians. That ties into routing policies and Redwood Optimize's quality monitoring.
[05:10] Tom (Riverview): On compliance, can you confirm SOC 2 and how audit logs look for Private deployments?
[05:15] Alex: Yes - SOC2 plus audit logs with per-token request metadata. For Private we support KMS integration and HSM for key storage. We'll send SOC2 and the architecture doc.
[05:24] Nina: What about model updates - if you push a new quantized build, how do rollouts work?
[05:28] Maya: We support canary rollouts and A/B testing in the console. You can pin model versions and roll a fraction of traffic. If quality regresses, automatic fallback rules can route back to a pinned version. We surface regression alerts tied to eval prompt sets.
[05:45] [05:48] Jorge: For the POC, we want exportable benchmarks that match our footprint - 60% read-only notes, 40% triage prompts; average prompt length ~400 tokens.
[05:58] Maya: Noted. We'll run a POC benchmark with that distribution - we'll include p50/p95, throughput, and estimated cost.
[06:08] Alex: Quick demo on the Console's Optimize tab - it suggests batching (we showed B=8 earlier) and prefix caching for repetitive triage prompts. For example if many prompts share the same patient history prefix, KV caching reduces tokens generated and improves effective throughput.
[06:25] Dr. Sarah: Any gotchas for clinician language-medical abbreviations?
[06:29] Maya: We recommend building a prompt template and a short eval set of edge cases. Redwood Optimize can flag quality drift and we can add guardrails (e.g., terminologies list) to post-process outputs.
[06:40] Alex: Pricing nuance - Hosted listing shows estimated cost-per-1k tokens; Dedicated is priced by reserved GPU capacity plus a smaller per-token charge. We'll send a tailored quote.
[06:52] Tom: Can you email the compatibility matrix and the benchmark CSV?
[06:55] Alex: Yes - action item for Maya and me.
[06:57] [07:00] Maya: A quick note about compatibility matrix structure: columns are Model, Verified Quant Profile, Supported GPUs, Approx Mem, Best Use-case, Known caveats. We also annotate whether Fast Attention kernels are enabled for a given GPU and seq-len.
[07:18] Jorge: Sequence length - for longer discharge summaries (~1,200 tokens) how do numbers change?
[07:24] Maya: Tail latency increases since attention is O(n^2) in some parts; we optimize kernel selection for longer seq lengths and sometimes recommend segmentation with summarization cascade (chunk -> summarize -> collapse) to keep latency and cost manageable. We can show a 1,200-token benchmark for your POC.
[07:42] Dr. Sarah: How long to get a POC running?
[07:45] Alex: Usually 2 weeks to provision a Dedicated trial or spin up a private deployment; Hosted POC can start in a few days. We'll aim for 2-week POC per your ask.
[07:55] Nina: Networking - for Private we need a minimal set of egress rules. Can you provide the list?
[07:59] Maya: Yes - we'll provide the VPC peering and firewall rules doc. Action item for Alex to send.
[08:07] [08:10] Dr. Sarah: Anything else on model selection?
[08:12] Maya: To summarize model picks: if you need highest fidelity and lower p95: LlamaX-13B FP16 on H100. If you need a balance of cost and accuracy: LLM-quant-8B on A100 with Q4 profile. For low-cost batch or fallback: Mistral-7B on T4. We'll attach a one-sheet with recommended default profiles.
[08:34] Alex: Ok let's go through the explicit next steps - (1) we'll send pricing & cost model; (2) Maya will upload benchmark csv and compatibility matrix; (3) Jorge will send workload distribution; (4) schedule POC kickoff next Wed 11/18.
[08:48] Tom: 11/18 works for us.
[08:51] Alex: Great - thanks everyone. We'll follow up via email with the artifacts and calendar invite.
[08:58] [09:00] End of recording.

Notes: Transcription contains occasional minor mis-transcriptions (e.g., "KV cash" instead of "KV cache"). Shared artifacts: Deck (https://redwood.ai/deck/model-catalog), Compatibility sheet (https://redwood.ai/compatibility/riverview), Benchmark CSV (will be attached).
